title: Karma
paragraphs: “I fully understand the Heroes’ perspective. I intend to do my best to support that vision.”
“…I’ve already asked the people of Siltvelt to spread the word about this, you know.”

Father is seizing this opportunity to corner the people of Shieldfreeden with his words. The people of Shieldfreeden are breaking out in a cold sweat, as if to prove a point. This is exactly it, isn’t it? It means that if it weren’t for the words of Father—the Shield Hero—you’d have just ignored them! That’s beyond foolish.
“W-well… it’s all the fault of the Takt faction. As for the profit reporting in Shieldfreeden, we’ll address that later…”
“Well, that being the case, I’m counting on you.”

Father issued a threat with a slightly dismissive tone. It was a veiled threat implying he wouldn’t hold back from the fallout, and a warning that if they didn’t take this seriously, the country would be wiped out.

“Ah, you’re free to run away if you want, but if you do, I’ll go ahead and reshape the country as I see fit. Since you chose to stay in your seats instead of running, you must have some resolve, right?”
“Y-yes. It’s precisely because we feel the weight of responsibility for the nation that we’re here.”

“Well then, for the sake of the nation, you’ll have to endure the pain of draining the pus. If you try to sweep this under the rug just because you can’t bear it, I’ll simply excise the entire area where you’re standing, understand?”

With one eye half-closed and an overbearing demeanor, Father delivered the final threat to the people of Shieldfreeden, and their course of action was thus decided. But… how should I put it? It seemed the people of Shieldfreeden occasionally showed signs of not fully agreeing with Father’s arguments. There were countless examples, such as their refusal to change the terms of their rights.
“Then how do you plan to resolve the issue of postwar reparations?” Father pressed them several times.
For now, the meeting ended on that note, and the schedule for tomorrow was finalized.

As the sun set, after a small dinner gathering, we were all escorted to the section of the building where the highest-ranking officials reside to rest. Oh, of course, we’d conducted a preliminary investigation beforehand, and Yuki-chan and the others had also finished their checks to ensure there would be absolutely no enemy attacks. After seeing Father and the others to their rooms, I’ll go pick up Yuki-chan and the others, who are waiting in my room.

It seems there aren’t the same strict distinctions in Shieldfreeden as there were in Siltvelt regarding me and Father. So it’s no problem to go hang out right away. Father must be exhausted, so I’ll offer him some advice and let Yuki-chan and the others help him relax with their charm as Filolial ladies. I’m sure Sakura-chan is already doing this, but the more hands on deck, the better.

I’ll take Yuki-chan and the others to Father’s room, knock on the door, and go right in. Oh, of course, there are Siltvelt bodyguards and Shieldfreeden security guards stationed in front of the door, but with my free pass, I can get through with ease.
“Father! You must be tired today…”

Just as I was about to say that, I choked on my words. The reason being, I happened to catch a glimpse of Father having Panda remove his upper body armor and hugging him from behind, burying his face in his back. W-what on earth is going on here? Has Father already become that close with Panda?
“Uh, listen? Don’t get the wrong idea, okay? Even I don’t really understand what the Shield Hero is up to.”

“Hmm? Naofumi—just when I thought he’d come back to the room, he told Rasa to take off his armor, and once she did, he hugged her from behind. He said it was Sakura’s turn next, so I’m waiting for her.”
Father stayed clinging to the panda’s back for a while, but then he pulled away and looked at me.
“Ah, Motoyasu, what’s up?”
“No, I’m the one who should be asking—what’s going on with you, Father?”
“Hm? Oh… I’m just starting to feel a little tired… I thought maybe I could get away with doing this much, so I decided to give it a try.”
That’s not really an answer. No, you need to think deeper about this, Motoyasu. There must be some deeper reason behind Father’s actions. Hmmmm… Huh!?
“You want to get cozy with the panda, don’t you?”

It’s a good thing you two get along well. Even Father in this world needs a reliable partner of the opposite sex, just like your Older Sister. People become stronger when they have someone to protect… Just as I have my dear Filo, Father… no, it’s not just Father. Ren and Itsuki also changed because they formed connections with others. So let’s have the panda take on that role.
“After all that deep thinking, that’s it?! I’m telling you, that’s not it!”
For some reason, the panda is suddenly telling me that’s not right. But I’m talking to Father here! Final answer?
“No, no… It’s just been such a chaotic mess lately that I’m exhausted. I guess I was a little too high-handed trying to bridge the gaps in understanding with the people from Shieldfreeden.”

After all, Father had been talking nonstop for a long time during those meetings with the Shieldfreeden delegation. He’s actually a very kind person, so being harsh with others must have taken a toll on him.

Plus, he hadn’t had a proper break up until now. It’s been a nonstop series of battles ever since the war with Shieldfreeden began. First Faubrey, then Shieldfreeden… I can totally understand why he’s exhausted.

But when I think back on how he’s always been, he didn’t seem like the type to get tired over something like that… That’s what I thought at first, but then I pictured him in the first world, in the midst of a similarly grueling workload, gently petting the kind of monster my Older Sister had created—and the two images overlapped.

Speaking of the first world, I remember that shortly before you, Father, established your stronghold with Filo and the others at Older Sister’s residence, you looked particularly exhausted. Up until then, you’d been scolding people and devising all sorts of strategies to ensure everyone’s survival.

Even though it might have seemed like no big deal to me, perhaps he was feeling a growing sense of guilt. I suspect that incident was the result of Father’s conscience exploding under the stress of being harsh toward someone or maintaining order in the territory. After the world achieved peace, Father referred to it as a “hidden Karma stat,” and I tend to agree.
……Hmm? Memories of the first world are coming back to me. I’ve forgotten exactly when it was, but it’s a scene of Father talking to my Older Sister while looking in my direction.
“I wonder why Motoyasu doesn’t go on a rampage even as his karma increases.”
“There are still times when he does things that can’t be brushed off as a joke… Maybe he’s already gone off the rails?”
“That might be part of it, but why doesn’t the curse stack up…?”
“Did you call me?”
“I didn’t. Go home. And just stay put.”
“Got it!”
“It’s truly mysterious, isn’t it?”
“I suppose that’s just how people are…”

Thanks to Father, Big Sister, and the creature created from Big Sister, I don’t think anything like that has happened since. He must need some healing. I imagine Father is feeling a similar kind of fatigue right now. I suspect he has a habit of stroking fur to unconsciously relieve stress.
That’s a *sparkle*☆, isn’t it?

I see… So this was a habit unique to Father when he was feeling exhausted. The fact that he’s trying to do the same thing with Sakura-chan suggests he was secretly relying on someone he trusts. I’m sure he was doing something similar with Filo-tan, too!
Woooooooon! I’m so jealous!

Wait a minute, though. The one that Father was stroking in plain sight was the monster created by my Older Sister. Other than that, he’d at most just roughly stroke Keel here and there—nothing that stood out much… It kind of makes it seem like Father didn’t trust Lady Filolial in the first world… but that’s just my imagination! Father absolutely adores Lady Filolial!
“The Spear Hero is pulling all kinds of faces at us—what’s that all about?”
“I don’t know… It’s the same old thing, so I think it’s best not to worry about it too much.”
“I agree… By the way, how much longer do you plan on clinging to me?”
“Sorry, just a little longer.”
“Alright… I wonder if this counts as part of my job?”
“I feel like the people of Siltvelt are manipulating me pretty well, but please, just a little longer.”
“Fine, fine. Go ahead and cling to my back until you’re satisfied. If you’re tired, I guess there’s nothing I can do about it.”
And so, the panda goes along with Father, who seems to have given up and is clinging to her. Father is stroking the panda’s fur. It seems kind of silky to the touch.
“Isn’t a panda’s fur supposed to be coarse?”
“Huh? Oh, yeah, it was like that when we first met. But lately, it’s gotten quite soft, hasn’t it?”

“Well, that’s because she’s been entrusted with guarding the Shield Hero… The folks at the castle want everyone to stay clean and be a support to the Hero, so they’ve supplied her with top-of-the-line beauty products. On top of that, whenever she’s off duty, they force her to go to the spa. Even though it’s not my thing.”
“I see. That’s why your fur has become surprisingly soft.”
“It’s kind of unsettling that my fur’s gotten so soft for no reason. Plus, those guys keep trying to touch me under some pretext or another—it’s incredibly annoying.”
The “those guys” the panda is referring to are probably his subordinates. I’m holding down the fort over at Siltvelt. I heard they’re doing technical training to become even stronger.
“Can I change the subject, if that’s okay?”
“Of course.”

“It’s about Shieldfreeden. There’s this vibe that they have the upper hand in terms of resources and territory, and with their joint development with Takt and the others, their arsenal is fully equipped. It seems they were biding their time, waiting for an opportunity to defeat Siltvelt… You know, kind of like a certain country I know—they were so eager to go all out precisely because they resented Siltvelt, or perhaps because they wanted independence.”
Father begins explaining while hugging Panda. It’s a relaxed discussion. Since it’s a serious topic, I’m listening intently, too.

“There’s no doubt about it… Well, to be honest, when it comes to politics, as a mercenary, I’d actually prefer it if wars and the like broke out. But the folks in Shieldfreeden seemed a bit out of touch—or rather, like they didn’t understand reality. They share the same ‘might makes right’ philosophy as Siltvelt, but their way of thinking is different.”

Maybe he finally saw reality after Father’s threats—he was trembling throughout the meeting. He must have realized by now that defying us would cost him his life. As a result, it seemed like he was trying his best to protect his vested interests.

“As for the meeting… they’re showing determination to arrest the former representative and eradicate the Takt faction, but whenever it comes to other vested interests, they’re bound to latch on. I got tired of all the ‘first come, first served’ talk that kept popping up.”

“I understand how they feel, though,” Father added. “Well, the people from Shieldfreeden did seem a bit giddy. For better or worse, I think they were being led by the nose by Takt and lacked common sense.”
“You said, ‘Even if you manage to defend these rights to the death, how are you guys going to pay the compensation?’”

“Yeah. Even though we told them we couldn’t pay unless we used those profits toward the compensation, all we got were responses like requests to extend the deadline. And to top it off, they said things like, ‘Please wait—we have a strategy to generate new profits…’ It just felt like the worst aspects of democracy were on full display.”

Come to think of it, Shieldfreeden was a democracy, wasn’t it? Since most countries in this world are monarchies, decisions made by the head of state are usually carried out swiftly. As heroes, we’re in a position where it’s easy for us to voice our opinions to those in power. So, if we offer advice or make proposals to the Queen of Melromarc or the Pig King of Faubrey, we can move projects forward relatively easily.

In contrast, Shieldfreeden is a democracy. While there may be fewer failures, if you try to move something forward and there are opponents, you simply can’t act quickly. I suppose that’s what Father means by “the downsides.” Well, I’ve heard that in a monarchy, if the ruler is incompetent, the kingdom can collapse in the blink of an eye.
Oh? Memories of the first world are coming back to me. This is the issue that had Father, Ren, and Itsuki all sighing in unison.
“I recall that even in the first world, when peace was established, the waves caused the worlds to merge, and Shieldfreeden was the first to launch an invasion of the newly discovered continent.”

“Ah, so that’s what the ‘Wave’ phenomenon was? Thinking about it that way, it means they were trying to pay off the country’s debt—the reparations—using the goods and money they’d obtained through invasion.”

Incidentally, the same was true for Faubrey. Well, that was largely because Takt’s actions effectively led to Faubrey’s downfall. I recall that the people of Faubrey also tried to pay off their reparations through similar invasions, but the hawkish factions in both nations were wiped out by Father and his allies. That’s what you’d call a fitting punishment. That’s about all I remember.
